name: Underwrite private credit investments
summary: Credit Investments deal teams take a private credit opportunity that passed screening, usually a loan to a private equity sponsor-backed company or a structured or real asset financing, and underwrite it: data room review, a cash flow and recovery model, management and sponsor meetings, a term sheet negotiated against competing lenders, adviser diligence, tax, ESG and legal input, an internal rating and a credit memo. The department committee approves smaller credits and recommends larger ones to the Portfolio Execution Committee. About 40% of credits are lost to other lenders, declined or dropped. Sponsor timetables, adviser reports, inputs from other teams and memo edits take most of the elapsed time, and bespoke structures handled with little standardisation raise legal and operational risk.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager whose 137-person Credit Investments department lends directly and through partners across corporate, structured and real asset credit.
baseline.notes: Public credit trading is excluded (ci-public-credit-decisions). Final documentation and funding follow in lc-negotiate-close and private investment operations.

trigger: A screening memo recommending a private credit opportunity is approved and the team is invited to provide terms.
end_state: A credit memo is submitted to Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee or approved within department authority, or the credit is declined or lost.

volume.seasonality: Heavier in the autumn and before calendar year end when sponsors close buyouts; slower in the first months of the pandemic in 2020.

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Virtual data rooms run by sellers and advisors
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Compliance system for personal trading, attestations and restricted lists
Risk analytics platform (potential loss, limits, stress tests)

steps.name: Accept the screening memo and staff the deal team
steps.description: A Credit Investments director reads the approved screening memo, opens the credit in the deal pipeline, names a principal, senior associate, associate and analyst, and sets a workplan against the sponsor's or arranger's timetable.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common private credit practice.

steps.name: Clear conflicts and bring the team over the wall
steps.description: A compliance officer checks the borrower and sponsor against existing holdings, other deal teams and the restricted list, records the non-disclosure agreement, adds the borrower to the watch list and, where the borrower has public securities, restricts public credit trading by the team.

error.defect_description: Watch list entry missed for an affiliate.

control.basis: Insider trading law and the fund's information barrier policy separating private-side borrower information from public credit trading

evidence.note: CI invests in both public and private credit (F2021), which makes information barriers necessary; step content is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the data room and lender materials
steps.description: An associate works through the lender presentation, financial statements, the sponsor's quality of earnings and commercial reports, customer and contract data in the virtual data room, and logs questions and red flags.

error.defect_description: A risk in the documents is not logged.

evidence.note: Private credit borrowers are mostly sponsor-backed middle-market firms (FEDS); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send diligence questions and chase answers
steps.description: An analyst consolidates the question list, submits it through the data room or to the arranger, tracks open items and chases the borrower and sponsor for missing documents.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for borrower and sponsor answers
steps.description: The borrower, sponsor and their advisers answer questions, add documents and provide reliance on their diligence reports. Some processes are pulled or awarded to another lender at this stage.

next.condition: process pulled or lender chosen elsewhere

evidence.note: Waits and share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the credit model and downside cases
steps.description: A senior associate builds the cash flow model: revenue and margin drivers, leverage and interest coverage, free cash flow after capital spending, debt paydown, covenant headroom, enterprise value and recovery under base, downside and severe cases, including higher floating rates.

control.basis: Written, measurable underwriting standards with borrower stress testing (leveraged lending guidance as industry reference)

evidence.note: Clear written underwriting standards and stress tests (SR 13-3); floating rate loans and interest coverage near 2.0x (FEDS); fragile borrowers and layered leverage (IMF GFSR). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the model, leverage and recovery analysis
steps.description: The principal challenges the forecast, adjustments to earnings, leverage, coverage and recovery assumptions, compares them with similar credits in the book, and sends the model back for changes or clears it.

control.basis: Four-eyes review of credit analysis before committee

evidence.note: Rework share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Meet management and the sponsor
steps.description: The principal and senior associate meet the company's management and the private equity sponsor, test the business plan, use of proceeds and sponsor support, and write up the meeting notes.

evidence.note: Most private credit borrowers are sponsor-backed (FEDS); meeting timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Early-look committee approves the term sheet and diligence spend
steps.description: The group head and senior team review a short early-look paper with the credit case, proposed structure and pricing, and approve issuing a term sheet and spending on lender counsel and advisers, ask for more work or decline.

control.basis: CI delegated authorities under the investment policies, standards and procedures required by the fund's governing act s.35

evidence.note: The Act requires investment policies and procedures; the two-stage committee and shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the term sheet and structure
steps.description: The senior associate drafts the term sheet: facility type and seniority, size and hold, pricing and fees, amortisation, financial covenants or covenant-lite terms, security package, reporting and transfer rules, and shares it with Tax and Sustainable Investing for their reviews.

evidence.note: Terms set by bilateral negotiation; senior secured and floating rate structures (FEDS). Time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Negotiate terms with the sponsor or arranger
steps.description: The director negotiates pricing, leverage, covenants and documentation points with the sponsor or arranger against competing lenders' offers, and agrees terms in principle, revises the term sheet, or loses the deal.

next.condition: lost to another lender or terms rejected

evidence.note: Competition on speed, flexibility and covenants (IMF); borrowers pay for speed and certainty (FEDS). Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Engage lender counsel and diligence advisers
steps.description: An associate gets fee quotes, signs engagement letters with lender counsel and any appraiser, industry consultant or insurance adviser, sends scopes and data room access, and sets report dates.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Receive advisers' diligence reports
steps.description: Lender counsel, appraisers and consultants complete their work and send draft reports on legal structure and security, asset values or the market.

evidence.note: Report timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review adviser findings and update the model
steps.description: The senior associate reads the reports, updates the model and structure for new findings, and lists open issues that need terms changes or protections.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether to continue after diligence
steps.description: The director weighs the findings against the credit case and agreed terms, and decides to continue, reopen terms with the sponsor, or drop the credit.

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Integrate the tax structure memo and ESG assessment
steps.description: An associate collects the tax structure memo on withholding and holding entity choices and the sustainability assessment, including the climate framework where climate risk is material, chases them if late, and works their conclusions into the model and memo.

error.defect_description: Late tax change not carried into returns.

evidence.note: Climate framework applies to direct investments needing Portfolio Execution Committee approval (2022 report); waits are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review key legal terms and security
steps.description: In-house legal counsel reviews lender counsel's findings and the draft commitment papers or credit agreement, focusing on security, guarantees, covenants, transfer restrictions and any bespoke features, and sends comments.

control.basis: Legal review of bespoke transaction terms before commitment

evidence.note: Bespoke private credit transactions raise legal risk (F2022); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assign the internal credit rating and size the hold
steps.description: The senior associate scores the borrower with the internal rating model, compares it with the portfolio's target credit quality and concentration, and sets the proposed hold and any sell-down.

control.basis: Internal credit rating methodology and portfolio credit quality targets

evidence.note: CI targets a portfolio profile with average rating B+ (F2022); method and time are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the credit investment memo
steps.description: The senior associate writes the memo: borrower and sponsor, credit thesis, structure and terms, model cases, recovery, rating, tax, ESG and legal findings, risks and mitigants, returns and fit with the program mandate.

error.defect_description: Inconsistent numbers between memo and model.

evidence.note: Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and edit the memo
steps.description: The director reads the memo with the model, edits the thesis and risk sections, checks numbers against the model and term sheet, and sends it back for another draft or clears it.

control.basis: Senior review of investment memos before committee

evidence.note: Rework share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check approval authority, limits and sign-offs
steps.description: A CI business management associate checks which approval tier applies, that statutory issuer and related-party limits and program limits are met, that tax, ESG and legal sign-offs are attached, and that the memo uses the current template.

control.basis: The model fund Regulations s.11 (10% of assets in one issuer) and s.16 (related-party transactions); delegated authority limits

evidence.note: Statutory limits (Regulations); non-standard private credit processing (F2022). Share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Department investment committee decides
steps.description: The group head and senior members review the memo with the deal team, and approve it within department authority, recommend it to the Portfolio Execution Committee, send it back for more work, or decline it.

control.basis: CI delegated authorities under the fund's governing act s.35 investment policies

next.condition: recommend to the Portfolio Execution Committee

evidence.note: Share recommended to the committee is set so that about 8 CI memos a month reach it, matching pim-tf-pec-approval; other shares are estimates.

steps.name: Submit the memo to Risk and the committee secretariat
steps.description: An associate files the final memo and appendices in the memo repository, sends them to the Risk transaction review team and the Portfolio Execution Committee secretariat, and records the submission in the deal pipeline.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the department approval and hand over to closing
steps.description: An associate records the approval and conditions in the deal pipeline and memo repository, and notifies Legal, Tax, Risk and private investment operations so documentation, funding and booking can start.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Lost to another lender
exceptions.description: The sponsor or arranger picks a lender with better terms or more certainty, usually during term negotiation.

exceptions.name: Declined at early look
exceptions.description: The early-look committee declines before adviser spending starts.

exceptions.name: Dropped on diligence findings
exceptions.description: Adviser reports or management meetings reveal problems the terms cannot fix.

exceptions.name: Terms reopened after diligence
exceptions.description: Findings require re-pricing, tighter covenants or more security, so terms go back to the sponsor.

exceptions.name: Memo redrafts
exceptions.description: The director, the authority check or the committee sends the memo back for another draft.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from screening approval to memo submitted, department approval, decline or loss
benchmarks.population: Private credit underwriting at a large institutional direct lender

evidence.note: No published statistic. Author's estimate: completed credits take about five to eight weeks from term sheet request to committee, and lost or declined credits end earlier; borrowers pay for speed and certainty of execution (FEDS).
Net assets C$54 billion.

benchmarks.unit: average credit rating of the portfolio, fiscal 2022

evidence.note: Average credit rating of B+.
Around 2.0x versus about 2.7x for leveraged loan borrowers.

benchmarks.unit: share of par recovered after default

evidence.note: About 33% versus 52% for syndicated loans.
Topped US$2.1 trillion.

pain_points.description: Private credit transactions are processed with little standardisation and automation, so authority checks, sign-offs and hand-overs are manual and error-prone.

evidence.note: Moderate operational risk from lack of standardisation and automation (F2022).

pain_points.description: Bespoke structures need legal review and raise legal risk, and late legal points can reopen terms.

evidence.note: Increased legal risk from bespoke private credit transactions (F2022).

pain_points.description: Sponsors run competitive processes and expect quick, certain answers, so teams lose deals on terms and timing.

evidence.note: Competition on speed and covenants (IMF, FEDS).

pain_points.description: The memo waits for tax and ESG inputs from other teams that arrive late or change after structure changes.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file notes late structure changes force tax rework.

pain_points.description: Several rounds of memo edits between the senior associate, the director and the committee.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: The model fund F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)
sources.supports: Credit Investments invests in public and private credit across the capital structure, liquid/syndicated and direct; Americas Leveraged Finance invests in leveraged loans, unitranche loans, bridge financings, mezzanine debt and preferred equity and owns Antares Capital, a lender to middle-market private equity sponsors

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)
sources.supports: CI net assets C$54 billion, 137 full-time employees, average credit rating B+; moderate operational risk from lack of standardisation and automation in processing private credit transactions; increased regulatory and legal risk from the bespoke nature of some private credit transactions; returns attributed to underwriting discipline and partnerships

sources.title: 2022 Report on Sustainable Investing
sources.supports: Climate Change Security Selection Framework applied to any direct investment requiring Portfolio Execution Committee approval where climate risk is potentially material; structured reviews of material sustainability factors in diligence

sources.title: Private Credit: Characteristics and Risks (FEDS Notes)
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.supports: Private credit lends to middle-market firms with revenues of US$10 million to US$1 billion, mostly private equity sponsor-backed; terms set by bilateral negotiation, increasingly club deals; almost all floating rate; direct lending loans senior secured; mean interest coverage around 2.0x versus 2.7x for leveraged loan borrowers (2023); lenders hold loans to maturity or refinancing; borrowers pay for speed and certainty of execution and customisation; post-default value about 33% for direct loans

sources.title: Fast-Growing $2 Trillion Private Credit Market Warrants Closer Watch
sources.supports: Private credit topped US$2.1 trillion in assets and committed capital in 2023; borrowers are smaller and carry more debt than leveraged loan or bond issuers; growth driven by speed, flexibility and attentiveness to borrowers; competition with banks pressures underwriting standards and covenants

sources.title: Global Financial Stability Report, April 2024 (chapter on private credit)
sources.supports: Private credit traditionally provides loans to mid-sized firms outside banks and public debt markets; vulnerabilities include relatively fragile borrowers, multiple layers of leverage and stale, potentially subjective valuations

sources.title: SR 13-3: Interagency Guidance on Leveraged Lending
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.supports: Underwriting standards should be clear, written and measurable and reflect risk appetite; periodic loan- and portfolio-level stress tests on leveraged loans; regular reporting on the leveraged portfolio

sources.title: The model fund Regulations (SOR/99-190)
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
sources.supports: Section 11: no more than 10% of the book value of assets in securities of one person or associated persons; section 16: prohibition on transactions with related parties, with exceptions in section 17

sources.title: the fund's governing act (S.C. 1997, c. 40), sections 34 and 35
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
sources.supports: The board must establish investment policies, standards and procedures that a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in dealing with the property of others, and the Board must follow them

assumptions: The process starts when the screening memo is approved and ends at memo submission, department approval, decline or loss; final documentation and funding are in lc-negotiate-close and private investment operations.
A two-stage committee (early look, then department investment committee) is assumed as common practice; CI's actual committee structure and authority limits are not public.

The share recommended to the Portfolio Execution Committee is set so that about 8 CI memos a month reach it, matching the CI share assumed in pim-tf-pec-approval; about 15% of credits are approved within department authority.
The organisation file lists no output for credits approved within department authority; this workflow sends an approval_decision to lc-negotiate-close for them.

Due diligence reports, tax structure memos and ESG assessments arrive during a case and are standing inputs, not triggers; term sheets go to Tax and Sustainable Investing for every credit that reaches s10.
compliance_officer and legal_counsel are organisation roles not listed for this process; they are added for wall-crossing and legal review.
Hands-on times count focused work; stated FTE is a little above the implied FTE because deal teams also spend unrecorded time on calls, travel and amendments to existing loans.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file and include large incentive pay.
